sem.oneIdea: IP Security at the network layer, the two modes (transport and tunnel), the two security protocols (AH and ESP), what each protects, and how they compare.
sem.keyVisual:
Exam strategy

“Explain transport and tunnel mode” and “compare AH and ESP” are guaranteed questions. Know: AH = authentication only, ESP = authentication + encryption. Transport = end-to-end, tunnel = gateway-to-gateway.

sem.subject: Info & Data Security
sem.title: Security Association, Security Policy and IKE
sem.deck: Security Associations (SA) and their parameters, the Security Policy Database (SPD), the Security Association Database (SAD), and Internet Key Exchange (IKE) phases.
sem.oneIdea: Security Associations (SA) and their parameters, the Security Policy Database (SPD), the Security Association Database (SAD), and Internet Key Exchange (IKE) phases.
sem.keyVisual:
Exam strategy

“What is a Security Association?” and “Explain IKE” are standard 5-mark questions. Know: SA = one-way, identified by SPI + destination + protocol. IKE has two phases.

sem.subject: Info & Data Security
sem.title: System Security and Threat Models
sem.deck: Description of system security architecture, security assets, threats vs vulnerabilities, security policy and mechanisms, and the STRIDE threat modeling framework.
sem.oneIdea: Description of system security architecture, security assets, threats vs vulnerabilities, security policy and mechanisms, and the STRIDE threat modeling framework.
sem.keyVisual:
Exam strategy

“Describe the fundamental concepts of system security: assets, threats, vulnerabilities, and security controls” is a standard introductory 5-to-8 mark question. Distinguish clearly between a threat (potential harm), a vulnerability (flaw), and an attack (exploitation of flaw).

sem.subject: Info & Data Security
sem.title: Buffer Overflow and Memory Attacks
sem.deck: Memory layout of a running process, stack frame mechanics, smashing the stack, return address hijacking, shellcode injection, NOP sleds, and modern hardware/compiler defenses (Canaries, ASLR, DEP/NX).
sem.oneIdea: Memory layout of a running process, stack frame mechanics, smashing the stack, return address hijacking, shellcode injection, NOP sleds, and modern hardware/compiler defenses (Canaries, ASLR, DEP/NX).
sem.keyVisual:
Exam strategy

“Explain buffer overflow with stack diagram, shellcode injection, and countermeasures” is a guaranteed 10-mark question. Draw the stack layout clearly, showing the direction of buffer growth (low to high memory) toward the saved frame pointer and saved return address.

sem.subject: Info & Data Security
sem.title: Malicious Software — Viruses, Worms, Trojans
sem.deck: Taxonomy of malware, virus lifecycle and evasion strategies (polymorphic vs metamorphic), worm propagation mechanics, Stuxnet, Trojan horses, rootkits, ransomware, and botnets.
sem.oneIdea: Taxonomy of malware, virus lifecycle and evasion strategies (polymorphic vs metamorphic), worm propagation mechanics, Stuxnet, Trojan horses, rootkits, ransomware, and botnets.
sem.keyVisual:
Exam strategy

“Differentiate between a virus and a worm” and “Explain the phases of a virus and how polymorphic viruses evade detection” are guaranteed 7-to-10 mark questions. Always structure answers with the standard 4 phases and include comparison tables.

sem.subject: Info & Data Security
sem.title: Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS)
sem.deck: Architecture of intrusion detection systems, signature-based vs anomaly-based detection, HIDS vs NIDS deployment, honeypots, and Snort rule anatomy.
sem.oneIdea: Architecture of intrusion detection systems, signature-based vs anomaly-based detection, HIDS vs NIDS deployment, honeypots, and Snort rule anatomy.
sem.keyVisual:
Exam strategy

“Compare Signature-based vs Anomaly-based IDS” and “Differentiate HIDS and NIDS with advantages and disadvantages” are standard 8-to-10 mark exam questions. Provide clear side-by-side tables and explain false positives vs false negatives.

sem.subject: Info & Data Security
sem.title: Firewalls and Virtual Private Networks (VPN)
sem.deck: Perimeter defense architectures, packet filtering vs stateful vs application proxy firewalls, DMZ topologies, bastion hosts, and VPN tunneling protocols (IPSec and SSL/TLS).
sem.oneIdea: Perimeter defense architectures, packet filtering vs stateful vs application proxy firewalls, DMZ topologies, bastion hosts, and VPN tunneling protocols (IPSec and SSL/TLS).
sem.keyVisual:
Exam strategy

“Compare Packet Filtering, Stateful Inspection, and Application Gateway Firewalls” and “Explain DMZ architecture and Bastion Host with neat diagram” are 10-mark staples. Always detail the layer of operation, state table tracking, and performance trade-offs.
